question: Luria and Delbrück exposed many bacterial cultures to a virus. What did the wildly uneven survivor counts show?
options: The virus triggered resistance in some cells
Survivors had simply dodged the virus
Resistance arose by chance before exposure
answer: Resistance arose by chance before exposure. Had the virus induced resistance, every culture would have held a similar small number of survivors. Instead most had none and a few had hundreds, as expected if a random mutation struck early in some cultures and then multiplied. Mutations do not arrive because they are needed.
move: Variation comes first; a challenge only reveals who already had the answer.
ask: When the next crisis hits, which of the skills I am building now will turn out to matter?
trap: Need seems to call forth the change, as if bacteria adapt on demand.
reference: Luria & Delbrück, Mutations of bacteria from virus sensitivity to virus resistance, Genetics, 1943
